marco: Idea: try an "adaptive-redaction" policy that combines a privacy_score (0-100) with sampling guardrails. high-level: privacy_score >= 85 => redact, 60-85 => pseudonymize, <60 => keep but only to traced sample streams. goal is fewer false positives than blanket redact and clearer debug signal.

lily: I like a score instead of raw confidence since we can fold in heuristics (PII model, entity entropy, route sensitivity). how do we compute route sensitivity?

marco: route sensitivity = base_route_tier + tenant_flags + recent-incident-penalty. simple numeric add. e.g., login route +30, support-v1 +10.

sam: couple infra constraints: any time we *keep* cleartext we must 1) only send to sampled collectors, 2) store only in ephemeral inspector (signed URL + expiry), 3) encrypt at rest. also need a per-tenant opt-out.

sec-dev: security checklist: signed audit trail for every inspector access, per-access notifyable webhook to compliance, use HSM for salt rotation keys. ops-bot: "audit-event: inspector-request-423"

marco: proposed sampling guardrail: if route sample_rate < 0.001, then do NOT allow cleartext branch; instead force pseudo or redact. prevents tiny-sample routes leaking PII.

lily: console needs to surface a new metric: approx_unmasked_count (estimated number of requests that would have been unmasked under <60). that should be computed daily and projectable via rollout modal.

sam: rollout plan: feature-flagged as agent.adaptive_redact v1. Phase 1: internal tenants only 100% for 72h (smoke). Phase 2: 10% of external production routes for 48h with strict alerts. Phase 3: gradual to 50% then 100%. auto-rollback if approx_unmasked_count > threshold or inspector_access_rate spikes.

marco: config sketch (proto) for per-route policy: 

```
route: /v1/chat
adaptive_redact:
  enabled: true
  score_bounds: {redact: 85, pseudo: 60}
  min_sample_rate_for_cleartext: 0.001
  pseudo_hash_mode: deterministic_salted
  inspector: {sample_rate: 0.005, ttl_seconds: 3600}
  audit_webhook: https://hooks.redwood/incoming/audit
```

sec-dev: question: deterministic_salted + rotating-salt means prior hashes break. we should either keep a lookback table for old salts for 14d or accept losing correlation. Prefer lookback table behind KMS, access-limited.

lily: UX: rollout modal should show a simulated "what-if" graph for last 7 days using stored detector outputs. show: daily projected inspector events, projected redact_rate delta, projected token cost. add a checkbox: "calculate using historical detector outputs (may take up to 30s)".

sam: telemetry hooks: emit these metrics per-route: adaptive.redact.score_histogram, adaptive.redact.action_counts{redact,pseudo,clear}, adaptive.redact.inspector_requests. add an alert rule: inspector_requests > expected * 2 && tenant not flagged -> page eng-oncall.

marco: also add a special case for regulated tenants: field force_mode: always_redact. config inherits from tenant profile.

sec-dev: retention rules: cleartext in inspector must be auto-scrubbed at TTL. pseudonymized mapping entries expire after 30d. any permanent retention must go through legal signoff.

ops-bot: "deploy: feature-flag agent.adaptive_redact enabled for internal tenants. canary id=adpt-17946"

lily: next steps: marco will open RFC + PR for detector hook + policy eval. sam will add telemetry plumbing and alerts. sec-dev will draft minimal audit webhook contract. I'll mock console "what-if" screens.

marco: sweet. small follow-up: need to decide whether privacy_score computation happens in preprocessor (fast quantized model + heuristics) or as a post-processing step in inference workers. I vote preprocessor so routing decisions are cheap.

sam: agree preprocessor. just ensure it's on fast path and cheap (<1ms p95). also add a fallback where if detector fails we default to pseudonymize.

marco: cool. thanks. I'll schedule RFC review for tomorrow. :raccoon:
